text:
emma: Heads-up, perf alert from canary: 95th latency for llama-13b-quant on p4d jumped ~2.1x after yesterday's kernel-selector change.
sam: saw that. Is it the kernel switch or the new batching heuristic?
emma: preliminary profiling points at KV cache eviction / refill spikes correlating with larger head dims for this variant.
oliver: dropped some perf counters into the CI job: cache_misses spiked when sequence > 1024 and batch > 8.
ci-bot: CI profile uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/profiles/1805001111/kv-evict-1805001111.pbz :zap:
nina: can you paste the hot function traces?
emma: here, truncated stack from perf: 
```
55.3% runtime: kernel_selector::select_best_kernel()
18.2% runtime: kv_cache::evict_and_refill()
9.7% runtime: batching::build_contiguous_batches()
4.1% runtime: rmsnorm::apply()
```
raj: interesting that select_best_kernel is top. Did the selector change its scoring weights?
sam: we bumped preference for fused-attn kernels to favor lower memory footprint; might be less optimal for higher head_dim models.
oliver: confirmed: the fused kernel avoids a second pass over KV which reduces memory but increases compute for larger head dims. That explains head-dim sensitivity.
nina: does this map to rope_theta scaling or hidden_size? The model here is Llama-3-13B with nonstandard head_dim=128 (vs 96 baseline).
emma: yes — head_dim up -> per-head matmul grows, and the fused kernel's tiling isn't great for that shape.
raj: KV eviction spike: when batch becomes heterogeneous (some long seqs, some short) our batching heuristic concatenates and evicts more aggressively. Need smarter backpressure.
sam: proposal: 1) revert kernel-selector weight change for prod 2) add quick heuristic: split batches by head_dim-tile compatibility and seq-length buckets 3) throttle KV eviction frequency for mixed batches
oliver: quick experiment script i ran: 
```
# run with old selector weights
./bench --model llama-13b-quant --kernels=legacy --batch=12 --seq=128,1024 --profile
```
result: 95p latency back down to ~1.05x baseline.
ci-bot: ab_test created: revert-kernel-selector-1805001150 (canary -> 2 pods)
nina: we should also log per-request kernel choice + head_dim in telemetry to catch regression earlier. Add a lightweight tag in the request trace.
emma: agreed. I'll open a quick PR to attach kernel_choice and head_dim to trace metadata.
raj: for longer term: tune kernel selector to consider head_dim and seq_len together, and add a small cost model for KV eviction. Also consider a fallback path that does per-request micro-batching when heterogeneity detected.
sam: ok let's do revert + telemetry + batch-split heuristic as short-term mitigations. Who can own the revert?
emma: i'll own revert and the PR for trace tags.
oliver: i'll prototype batch-split heuristic and run nightly bench.
nina: i'll add a dash widget to surface kernel_choice distribution per cluster.
ci-bot: rollout started: revert-kernel-selector-1805001150 -> canary 2/2 pods (started at 1805001160)
emma: thanks. follow-up: schedule an eng-runtime deep-dive tomorrow 10am PT to review perf signals and plan tuning milestones. :calendar: 
sam: +1. bring profiling snapshots and the old vs new kernel perf tables.
raj: thanks everyone — this explains the regression pattern we saw across a few customers.
ci-bot: canary healthy at 1805001188, 95p latency trend shows downward slope.
emma: closing the loop here — will post PR links and bench numbers in this thread once done. :thumbsup:
